docs.title: pyramids-mesh
docs.text: Reads and writes the file formats of hydrodynamic and hydraulic mesh models — 2DM, Selafin, DFSU, XMDF, PLY and more — as pyramids UGRID objects. pyramids-gis already ships the mesh data model and every operation that follows from a topology in hand; what it cannot do is open other people's mesh files. That is this package's only job.

docs.title: The layer boundary
docs.text:
The split is the point of the package, so it is worth stating precisely. pyramids-gis owns the mesh data model and everything that follows from a topology already in hand:

Concern Lives in Mesh2d, Network1d, UgridDataset, Connectivity pyramids.netcdf.ugrid UGRID-compliant NetCDF read / write pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.io Connectivity derivation, graph algorithms, boundary extraction pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.graph Sampling, rasterize_like, mesh-to-mesh regridding, time interpolation pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.regrid Construction from a raster grid or a polygon layer pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.construct Mesh ↔ vector, gap filling, xarray / zarr hand-off pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.{vector_ops,fill,interop_xarray} Mesh rendering pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.plot → cleopatra MeshGlyph

pyramids-mesh adds the one thing that is missing from that list — the ability to open other people's mesh files:

Concern Lives in Reading 2DM, Selafin, DFSU, XMDF, XDMF, DAT, FLO-2D, 3Di, PLY, TIN, … pyramids_mesh.drivers Writing 2DM, Selafin, DAT, PLY, Mike21 pyramids_mesh.drivers Driver discovery via the pyramids.mesh_drivers entry points pyramids-gis reads, this package registers

A survey of MDAL — the library QGIS uses for mesh layers — found pyramids-gis reads exactly one of its eighteen driver families (UGRID NetCDF). The other seventeen are what this package is for. In the other direction MDAL performs no interpolation, regridding, reprojection or graph analysis, all of which pyramids-gis already has.

Anything that belongs on the left-hand side of the first table is a change to pyramids-gis, not a feature of this package. Report it upstream rather than duplicating it here.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
0.1.0 is the repository scaffold — packaging, CI, docs, and the import contract that pins import pyramids first so the vendored osgeo bindings are active before anything else loads. The public surface is empty; pyramids_mesh.__version__ is all it exports.

>>> import pyramids_mesh
>>> pyramids_mesh.__version__
'0.1.0'

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
A primary goal of Hapi is to be inclusive to the largest number of contributors, with the most varied and diverse backgrounds possible. As such, we are committed to providing a friendly, safe and welcoming environment for all, regardless of gender, sexual orientation, ability, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and religion (or lack thereof).

This code of conduct outlines our expectations for all those who participate in our community, as well as the consequences for unacceptable behavior.

We invite all those who participate in Hapi to help us create safe and positive experiences for everyone.

docs.title: 2. Open [Source/Culture/Tech] Citizenship
docs.text:
A supplemental goal of this Code of Conduct is to increase open [source/culture/tech] citizenship by encouraging participants to recognize and strengthen the relationships between our actions and their effects on our community.

Communities mirror the societies in which they exist and positive action is essential to counteract the many forms of inequality and abuses of power that exist in society.

If you see someone who is making an extra effort to ensure our community is welcoming, friendly, and encourages all participants to contribute to the fullest extent, we want to know.

docs.title: 3. Expected Behavior
docs.text:
The following behaviors are expected and requested of all community members:

  • Participate in an authentic and active way. In doing so, you contribute to the health and longevity of this community.
  • Exercise consideration and respect in your speech and actions.
  • Attempt collaboration before conflict.
  • Refrain from demeaning, discriminatory, or harassing behavior and speech.
  • Be mindful of your surroundings and of your fellow participants. Alert community leaders if you notice a dangerous situation, someone in distress, or violations of this Code of Conduct, even if they seem inconsequential.
  • Remember that community event venues may be shared with members of the public; please be respectful to all patrons of these locations.

docs.title: 4. Unacceptable Behavior
docs.text:
The following behaviors are considered harassment and are unacceptable within our community:

  • Violence, threats of violence or violent language directed against another person.
  • Sexist, racist, homophobic, transphobic, ableist or otherwise discriminatory jokes and language.
  • Posting or displaying sexually explicit or violent material.
  • Posting or threatening to post other people's personally identifying information ("doxing").
  • Personal insults, particularly those related to gender, sexual orientation, race, religion, or disability.
  • Inappropriate photography or recording.
  • Inappropriate physical contact. You should have someone's consent before touching them.
  • Unwelcome sexual attention. This includes, sexualized comments or jokes; inappropriate touching, groping, and unwelcomed sexual advances.
  • Deliberate intimidation, stalking or following (online or in person).
  • Advocating for, or encouraging, any of the above behavior.
  • Sustained disruption of community events, including talks and presentations.

docs.title: 5. Weapons Policy
docs.text: No weapons will be allowed at Hapi events, community spaces, or in other spaces covered by the scope of this Code of Conduct. Weapons include but are not limited to guns, explosives (including fireworks), and large knives such as those used for hunting or display, as well as any other item used for the purpose of causing injury or harm to others. Anyone seen in possession of one of these items will be asked to leave immediately, and will only be allowed to return without the weapon. Community members are further expected to comply with all state and local laws on this matter.

docs.title: 6. Consequences of Unacceptable Behavior
docs.text:
Unacceptable behavior from any community member, including sponsors and those with decision-making authority, will not be tolerated.

Anyone asked to stop unacceptable behavior is expected to comply immediately.

If a community member engages in unacceptable behavior, the community organizers may take any action they deem appropriate, up to and including a temporary ban or permanent expulsion from the community without warning (and without refund in the case of a paid event).

docs.title: 7. Reporting Guidelines
docs.text:
If you are subject to or witness unacceptable behavior, or have any other concerns, please notify a community organizer as soon as possible. .

Additionally, community organizers are available to help community members engage with local law enforcement or to otherwise help those experiencing unacceptable behavior feel safe. In the context of in-person events, organizers will also provide escorts as desired by the person experiencing distress.

docs.title: 8. Addressing Grievances
docs.text: If you feel you have been falsely or unfairly accused of violating this Code of Conduct, you should notify with a concise description of your grievance. Your grievance will be handled in accordance with our existing governing policies.

docs.title: 9. Scope
docs.text:
We expect all community participants (contributors, paid or otherwise; sponsors; and other guests) to abide by this Code of Conduct in all community venues--online and in-person--as well as in all one-on-one communications pertaining to community business.

This code of conduct and its related procedures also applies to unacceptable behavior occurring outside the scope of community activities when such behavior has the potential to adversely affect the safety and well-being of community members.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This page covers installation of pyramids-mesh and its native dependencies.

Item Value Distribution name pyramids-mesh Python import name pyramids_mesh Current version 0.1.0 Supported Python 3.11 – 3.14 License GPL v3

Not published yet. 0.1.0 exists only in this repository — there is no PyPI or conda-forge release to install from. Use the from-source route below.

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
• pyramids-gis >= 0.68.0 (provides the pyramids import and the mesh-driver registry; pulled from PyPI)
  • numpy >= 2.0.0

GDAL is deliberately absent from that list. It is not a dependency of this package: the pyramids-gis wheel vendors its own osgeo bindings, and import pyramids is what puts them on sys.path. Nothing here installs or pins a separate GDAL.

scipy, shapely and geopandas are not declared either. The UGRID subsystem requires all three, so they arrive with pyramids-gis — but that is its requirement, not a promise to this package. Each gets declared here the moment a module under src/pyramids_mesh/ imports it directly.

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text: Extra Purpose Pulls viz mesh rendering / colour tables pyramids-gis[viz], cleopatra[tiles]

docs.title: Development dependency groups
docs.text:
dev, docs and notebook are PEP 735 dependency groups, not extras — they are local tooling and are deliberately not published in the package metadata. Pixi resolves a group by name wherever an environment lists it, so an environment is a set of groups and extras rather than a single same-named group: dev is py314 + dev + viz, docs is py314 + docs. notebook is currently referenced by no environment.

pixi install -e dev      # tests, linting, build tooling
pixi install -e docs     # mkdocs toolchain

docs.title: Recommended: Pixi
docs.text:
This repository ships a Pixi configuration that resolves every dependency from PyPI, GDAL included — the pyramids-gis wheel vendors its own, so no conda channel is involved and the usual GDAL-wheel headaches do not arise.

Prerequisites: install Pixi.

git clone https://github.com/serapeum-org/pyramids-mesh.git
cd pyramids-mesh

# Solve and install the dev environment
pixi install -e dev

# Drop into a shell with everything available
pixi shell -e dev

# Or run a task directly
pixi run main          # main test suite
pixi run plot          # plot/visualization tests
pixi run test-all      # everything, with a terminal coverage report
pixi run notebooks     # validate example notebooks

docs.title: Available Pixi environments
docs.text:
Environment Features Purpose default py314 minimal runtime dev py314, dev, viz tests, linting, build tooling docs py314, docs docs site (mkdocs serve) py311 py311, dev, viz pinned Python 3.11 py312 py312, dev, viz pinned Python 3.12 py313 py313, dev, viz pinned Python 3.13 py314 py314, dev, viz pinned Python 3.14

default, dev and docs are not unpinned — they reuse the py314 feature, so they resolve Python 3.14 like the matrix environment of that name. viz is a PEP 621 extra; dev, docs and notebook are PEP 735 dependency groups. The definitions live in pyproject.toml under [tool.pixi.environments].

The 3.13 and 3.14 pins carry a build glob (*_cp313 / *_cp314) that excludes the free-threaded interpreter: pyramids-gis ships no cp313t / cp314t wheel, and with no conda GDAL underneath, resolving one of those would fail at import rather than at solve time.

docs.title: Where the environments live
docs.text: .pixi/config.toml sets detached-environments to C:/python-environments/pixi/envs, keeping the multi-GB solved environments off the Google-Drive-synced checkout. That file is local-only (pixi writes a .pixi/.gitignore holding *), so each machine chooses its own location; without it, pixi puts the environments in .pixi/envs/ inside the repository.

docs.title: Editable / development install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/serapeum-org/pyramids-mesh.git
cd pyramids-mesh
pixi install -e dev
pixi run -e dev pre-commit install

The package itself is registered as an editable pixi pypi-dependency, so pixi install -e dev already puts your checkout on the path — there is no separate editable-install step.

>>> pyramids_mesh.__version__
'0.1.0'

• pyramids (conda-forge name) and pyramids-gis (PyPI name) are the same package. pyramids-mesh depends on the PyPI distribution name (pyramids-gis) so it works regardless of how pyramids itself was installed.

docs.title: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
docs.text:
This section collects significant architectural decisions for the pyramids-mesh project, using the MADR format.

  • ADR-0001: Documentation stack
  • ADR-0002: Type checking approach
  • ADR-0003: Scope boundary with pyramids-gis — superseded by 0005
  • ADR-0004: Versioned documentation strategy
  • ADR-0005: pyramids-mesh is a file-format driver package

Each ADR includes context, decision, and consequences. New ADRs should follow the numbering convention and be immutable once accepted.

docs.title: ADR-0001: Documentation stack
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-13

docs.title: Context
docs.text: We need a robust, contributor-friendly documentation stack that supports API reference, diagrams, tutorials, and versioned publishing — and that matches the rest of the stack, so a contributor moving between repositories does not relearn it.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Use MkDocs with the Material theme as the primary docs framework.
  • Use mkdocstrings[python] for auto-generating API reference from docstrings.
  • Prefer Mermaid fenced blocks for diagrams; allow PlantUML if complexity requires it.
  • Use mike to publish versioned documentation on GitHub Pages.
  • Execute example notebooks ahead of time and render their stored outputs (mkdocs-jupyter with execute: false); pixi run notebooks is what proves they still run.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Contributors document code with Google-style docstrings.
  • Diagrams render client-side in the site; heavy diagrams can be split or pre-rendered if needed.
  • CI builds the docs on pull requests, pushes to main, and releases, publishing with mike.

docs.title: ADR-0002: Type checking approach
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-13

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Static analysis improves reliability and developer experience, but the runtime stack underneath this package (GDAL via the vendored osgeo bindings, and the UGRID types it extends) is only partially typed, so full strictness is not reachable from day one.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Adopt gradual typing with standard Python type hints; annotate public APIs first.
  • mypy is installed in the dev group and may be run by contributors; it is not enforced in CI yet.
  • Prefer Google-style docstrings with type annotations to improve mkdocstrings output.
  • Mesh topology arrays are annotated with numpy.typing.NDArray, matching how pyramids annotates the same arrays, so signatures line up across the boundary.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Type hints are added progressively rather than in one sweep.
  • Strictness can be enabled per-module later, and a type-coverage report added to CI, without reworking existing annotations.

docs.title: ADR-0003: Scope boundary with pyramids-gis
docs.text:
• Status: Superseded by ADR-0005
  • Date: 2026-10-13

Superseded 2026-10-13. The three-concerns decision below (generation, quality, refinement) was written during scaffolding and was not the intended scope. This package is a file-format driver package; see ADR-0005, which restates every boundary rule from this ADR unchanged. Kept for the record; do not act on its Decision section.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
pyramids-gis already ships UGRID support in pyramids.netcdf.ugrid: the data model (Mesh2d, Network1d, UgridDataset, Connectivity), UGRID-compliant NetCDF I/O, connectivity derivation and graph algorithms, sampling and mesh-to-mesh regridding, construction by flattening a raster grid or a polygon layer, mesh-to-vector conversion, gap filling, spatial indexing, and rendering through cleopatra. This repository exists because three things are missing from that list, not because the mesh model needs a second implementation.

Without a stated boundary, the obvious failure mode is re-deriving connectivity or re-wrapping the NetCDF I/O here, which gives the stack two mesh types that drift apart.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• pyramids-gis remains the single owner of the mesh data model, its persistence, and every operation that follows from a topology already in hand. This package imports those types; it never redefines them.
  • pyramids-mesh owns three concerns:
    • Generation — producing a topology where none exists yet (as opposed to flattening a grid or polygon layer that already carries one, which is ugrid.construct).
    • Quality — per-element metrics (aspect ratio, skewness, orthogonality) and quality-driven smoothing.
    • Refinement — local refinement and coarsening of an existing mesh.
  • Public functions take and return pyramids.netcdf.ugrid types, so a result can go straight back into a UgridDataset and be written as UGRID NetCDF without a conversion step.
  • A gap or bug on the pyramids side of the boundary is reported and fixed upstream. A local workaround, if one is unavoidable, carries a comment naming the upstream issue and is removed when that lands.
  • Plotting goes through cleopatra, reached via pyramids — this package declares no plotting code of its own beyond the viz extra.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The dependency floor (pyramids-gis >= 0.66.0) is an API floor: raising it is the normal way to pick up an upstream mesh fix.
  • Some features will be rejected here and routed upstream instead; the table in the docs home page is the quick test for which side a concern falls on.
  • Interoperability is free — anything this package produces is already a UGRID mesh that the rest of the stack reads.

docs.title: ADR-0004: Versioned documentation strategy
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-13

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Readers need documentation matching the version they have installed, and contributors need to preview docs changes on a pull request before they merge.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Use mike to publish versioned docs to GitHub Pages.
  • Track main as the development version; publish releases under their tag and alias latest.
  • Publish pull-request previews through the shared mkdocs-deploy action's pull_request trigger.
  • The release tag comes from pyproject.toml's version, which commitizen bumps — one source of truth for the package version, the git tag, and the docs version selector.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Contributors update docs alongside code and see a preview on the pull request.
  • Users browse historical docs aligned with releases.
  • A release that skips cz bump publishes docs under the wrong version, so version bumps stay commitizen-driven.

docs.title: ADR-0005: pyramids-mesh is a file-format driver package
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-13
  • Supersedes: ADR-0003

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR-0003 scoped this package to mesh generation, quality and refinement. That scope was written during scaffolding, before the gap analysis it was meant to serve, and it does not match the work this repository exists to do.

The actual gap is format breadth. A survey of MDAL — the Mesh Data Abstraction Library that QGIS uses, and the reference implementation in this space — found that pyramids-gis reads exactly one of MDAL's eighteen driver families: UGRID NetCDF. The other seventeen are the native file formats of hydrodynamic and hydraulic solvers — SMS, TUFLOW, TELEMAC, DHI MIKE, FLO-2D, 3Di, ANUGA, HEC-RAS — and none of them can be opened today.

That survey also found the comparison runs the other way for everything else: MDAL performs no interpolation, regridding, reprojection, contouring, gap filling, mesh-to-vector conversion or graph analysis. pyramids-gis already has all of it. So the only substantial capability MDAL has over this stack is the ability to open other people's mesh files.

Reading a format is never out of scope for the stack, but seventeen parsers do not belong in pyramids-gis itself: they carry dependencies the core must not take (mikeio alone pulls pandas, matplotlib, scipy and tqdm), and their test fixtures are binary files measured in megabytes against a PyPI project that already refills its 10 GB limit roughly every twelve releases.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
pyramids-mesh reads and writes the file formats of hydrodynamic and hydraulic mesh models — 2DM, Selafin, DFSU, XMDF, PLY and the rest of MDAL's driver table — as pyramids.netcdf.ugrid objects. It owns file-format drivers; every mesh operation belongs upstream in pyramids-gis.

  • Generation, quality and refinement are dropped, not deferred. They were not an intended scope. If mesh generation is wanted later it gets its own package and its own argument.
  • Drivers are discovered by pyramids-gis through the pyramids.mesh_drivers entry-point group. This package depends on pyramids-gis; pyramids-gis never imports this package. That registry shipped in pyramids-gis 0.68.0, which is this package's floor, so registered drivers are discovered and dispatched to.
  • Each driver is a class declaring name, long_name, suffixes, api_version and a capabilities set, implementing can_open and mesh_names — which pyramids calls on every driver whatever it declares — plus either read (a format carrying topology) or read_data (a results-only format such as DAT, XMDF or XDMF, which carries values but no mesh). Only read_mesh, needs_mesh, write_mesh and write_data gate behaviour upstream; read_data, lazy_data and multi_mesh are declarative and require no method of their own.
  • The one dependency-backed driver family lives behind an extra — [dhi] (mikeio) — and a driver whose extra is absent is skipped at discovery, so a bare install stays small and useful. Mesh reading itself is never delegated to a third-party mesh library: that is pyramids-gis's, and a generic capability missing there is added there. The [interchange] extra (meshio) was dropped for this reason; PLY and the TIN formats are parsed here. [hdf] (h5py) went the same way: HDF5 is read through the GDAL multidimensional API over the GDAL vendored in the pyramids-gis wheel, which supplies group traversal, attributes and typed reads. mikeio remains because DFSU and DFS2 are proprietary DHI containers with no portable alternative.
  • Test fixtures are hand-built minimal files, committed, and kept out of the built distribution. Nothing special is needed for that: setuptools' sdist does not collect tests/data/*, and the wheel is built from src/ only. Vendor sample files are fetched in CI behind a marker, never committed.

docs.title: The boundary (carried over from ADR-0003 unchanged)
docs.text:
Every rule below was correct in ADR-0003 and is restated here because that ADR is superseded in full. Only its three-concerns decision was wrong.

  • pyramids-gis remains the single owner of the mesh data model, its persistence, and every operation that follows from a topology already in hand. This package imports those types; it never redefines them.
  • Public functions take and return pyramids.netcdf.ugrid types, so a result can go straight back into a UgridDataset and be written as UGRID NetCDF without a conversion step.
  • A gap or bug on the pyramids side of the boundary is reported and fixed upstream. A local workaround, if one is unavoidable, carries a comment naming the upstream issue and is removed when that lands.
  • Plotting goes through cleopatra, reached via pyramids. This package declares no plotting code — and, with the viz extra removed, no plotting dependency either: a driver returns data, and the caller plots it.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The pyramids-gis floor is an API floor on the registry, not on the mesh model. The registry shipped in pyramids-gis 0.68.0, so the floor is now >= 0.68.0 and this package's entry points are live: a driver it registers is dispatched to. The earlier hold on publishing to PyPI — kept while the registry was unreleased and the entry points inert — is lifted.
  • Three concerns MDAL supports and pyramids-gis does not — ragged vertical levels (DataOnVolumes), per-timestep active/dry flags, and a dataset reference time — are upstream work. A driver meeting them carries the value through without fabricating data: it raises on a genuinely ragged vertical profile rather than padding it, and attaches an active mask as a sibling variable rather than folding it into the values as NaN.
  • DFS2 is a structured grid rather than a mesh, so it is the one in-scope format whose natural target is a raster Dataset. Whether it belongs here at all is deliberately left open.
  • The viz extra is removed, and generation/quality/refinement leave the documentation.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• planning/design.md — the full architecture: driver protocol, registry and dispatch, the model contract, per-format specifications, and the task plan.
  • planning/mdal-comparison.md — MDAL's driver table and the capability comparison this decision rests on.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The API surface of pyramids_mesh, generated from the docstrings by mkdocstrings.

What this package publishes is drivers, not an API you call directly. A driver is registered with pyramids-gis through the pyramids.mesh_drivers entry-point group, so installing this package is the whole integration: pyramids then dispatches a read of a format it does not handle itself to the driver that claims it.

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("domain.2dm")   # resolved to this package's 2dm driver

So the entry points below are the surface that matters, and each driver has its own page listing its suffixes, capabilities and documented limitations:

Driver Format Page 2dm SMS / TUFLOW 2DM mesh frame 2DM dat SMS ASCII results, attached to a mesh DAT mike21 DHI Mike21 mesh frame Mike21 selafin TELEMAC Selafin / Serafin Selafin sww ANUGA SWW (NetCDF) SWW ply Stanford PLY polygon PLY xmstin XMS / SMS TIN XMS TIN

The package root deliberately re-exports nothing (__all__ is empty): it carries __version__ and the import contract that activates the vendored osgeo bindings. Driver classes are reached by their module path — pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver — which is also how their entry points name them, though normal use goes through pyramids rather than importing them at all.

For the mesh data model itself — Mesh2d, Network1d, UgridDataset, connectivity, graph algorithms, regridding, mesh ↔ vector — see the pyramids UGRID reference. The split between the two is ADR-0005, which supersedes ADR-0003 in full.

docs.title: pyramids_mesh
docs.text:
Mesh file-format drivers for the pyramids stack.

pyramids-mesh reads and writes the file formats of hydrodynamic and hydraulic mesh models — 2DM, Selafin, DFSU, XMDF, PLY and the rest of MDAL's driver table — as pyramids.netcdf.ugrid objects. pyramids.netcdf.ugrid owns the UGRID data model (Mesh2d, Network1d, UgridDataset), its NetCDF I/O, and every operation that follows from a topology already in hand — connectivity and graph algorithms, regridding and sampling, gap filling, mesh-to-vector conversion, and construction from a raster or a polygon layer. What it cannot do is open other people's mesh files; that is this package's job, and its only job.

Drivers are discovered by pyramids-gis through the pyramids.mesh_drivers entry-point group, so UgridDataset.read_file("model.slf") resolves to a driver here once this package is installed. Dependency-backed drivers sit behind extras ([dhi]) and are skipped at discovery when their extra is absent. See ADR-0005 for the scope decision.

The package root deliberately re-exports nothing: it carries __version__ and the import contract that activates the vendored osgeo bindings, and that is all. Installing the package is the whole integration, so nothing here needs importing. A driver class is still reachable by its module path (pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver, which is how its entry point names it) for the rare case of wanting one directly.

Examples:

  • The root carries the installed version and nothing else. __all__ is empty because there is deliberately nothing to re-export:

    import pyramids_mesh pyramids_mesh.version.split(".")[0].isdigit() True pyramids_mesh.all []

  • A driver is reached by its module path, not from the root, and reports the suffixes it claims:

    from pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms import TwoDmDriver TwoDmDriver.name '2dm' TwoDmDriver.suffixes ('.2dm',)

docs.title: 2DM — SMS / TUFLOW mesh frame
docs.text:
The 2DM reader. Plain text, one record per line, and the reference implementation every other driver in this package follows.

Driver name 2dm Suffixes .2dm Capabilities read_mesh, read_data, multi_mesh read_data and multi_mesh are declarative — they describe the driver in info(drivers=True) and require no method. There is no read_data() to call: read_data here means the file carries values (material, elevation) that read returns alongside the topology. A results-only format declares needs_mesh instead and does implement the method. Extra required none Returns UgridDataset for the surface mesh, Network1d for the E2L network 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("domain.2dm")

docs.title: Files holding both a surface and a network
docs.text:
A 2DM may carry a surface mesh (E3T/E4Q/E6T), a 1D network (E2L), or both. The two are named separately, so mesh_names tells you what a file holds and mesh_name= picks one:

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import Network1d, UgridDataset

UgridDataset.mesh_names("domain.2dm")            # ['mesh2d', 'network1d']
mesh = UgridDataset.read_file("domain.2dm")      # the surface mesh
channels = Network1d.read_file("domain.2dm", mesh_name="network1d")   # the 1D network

Reading the surface of a file that also holds E2L elements warns that the network is not in that result and names this route. The E2L elements are a separate 1D topology, not the surface mesh's edges, so they are never folded into edge_node_connectivity.

docs.title: What it reads
docs.text:
Record Meaning MESH2D the header; the file's first significant line must be this ND <id> <x> <y> <z> a node. z becomes a node_z variable, not a coordinate E3T <id> <n1..n3> <mat> a triangular face E4Q <id> <n1..n4> <mat> a quadrilateral face E6T <id> <n1..n6> <mat> a six-node face, read as such E2L <id> <n1> <n2> <mat> a 1D line element NUM_MATERIALS_PER_ELEM <k> switches the parser to k material columns

Node and element ids are resolved through an id map rather than by assuming id == index + 1: 2DM ids may have gaps and may be out of file order, and a tool that renumbers a mesh produces exactly that. The node count is the number of ND records, never the highest id.

The material id becomes a face-located material variable. With NUM_MATERIALS_PER_ELEM k the extra columns become material_2 … material_k, for k from 1 to 16 — each column costs an array and a variable, and the count comes from an untrusted file, so a larger one is refused rather than allocated.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Every one of these is deliberate; none is a silent approximation.

  • E3L, E8Q and E9Q are refused, and the whole file with them, naming the element. MDAL does the same (Err_UnsupportedElement). Treating a mid-side or centre node as a corner would distort the element without any error, so no mapping is guessed.
  • E6T is kept as a six-node face. Its node order is corner, mid-side, corner, mid-side, corner, mid-side, so the hexagon through those points is the element outline; it is not demoted to its corner triangle.
  • One read returns one topology. UgridDataset and Network1d are separate types, so a file holding both is read twice, once per mesh_name (see above). Reading either half warns about what the other half leaves behind rather than omitting it silently.
  • No elevation coordinate. The pyramids mesh model is planar, so on the surface path z survives as a node-located node_z variable. Anything consuming the mesh geometry sees the planar projection.
  • A 1D read cannot carry z, variables or global attributes at all. [Network1d][pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.Network1d] holds a topology and a CRS and has no parameter for data, so reading the network half of a file reports each of those by name in a warning and returns without them. This is a pyramids-gis limitation, not a decision of this driver: it will be carried properly once Network1d has somewhere to put it.
  • No elevation is invented. If no ND record carries a z column, node_z is omitted entirely rather than filled with zeros a consumer could not tell from a real zero datum. A file whose ND records disagree about the z column is refused, since the ones without it would need a datum invented.
  • Records this driver does not model are skipped, as MDAL skips them: MESHNAME, the BEGPARAMDEF block and anything else beyond the nodes, elements and NUM_MATERIALS_PER_ELEM. One consequence is that a file naming its own mesh loses that name — the topology is always built as mesh2d.
  • A malformed record is refused, never guessed. A record short of the fields its keyword requires, a non-numeric coordinate, id or material, and a NUM_MATERIALS_PER_ELEM below one all raise and name the file and the record. An element short of its declared material columns is the one exception: the missing columns read as 0.0, because a writer omitting a trailing column is common and refusing the file would cost more than it buys.
  • Two nodes, faces or line elements sharing an id are refused: the connectivity would be ambiguous.
  • No CRS. 2DM carries none, so crs is always None; it is never inferred from the coordinate magnitudes.
  • Read-only for now. write_mesh arrives with the 2DM writer (task W1).
  • Values are read eagerly: the format is text, so there is nothing to defer and lazy_data is not declared.

docs.title: DAT — SMS ASCII results
docs.text:
The DAT reader. Plain text carrying values and no topology, so it is attached to a mesh you already have rather than opened on its own.

Driver name dat Suffixes .dat Capabilities needs_mesh, read_data needs_mesh is what makes read_data the entry point: there is no topology in the file, so the mesh has to come from the caller. read() refuses and names attach_data. Extra required none Returns the variables it read, merged onto the dataset by attach_data 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

dataset = UgridDataset.read_file("domain.2dm")
with_results = dataset.attach_data("depth.dat")

docs.title: The element-count check is the whole safeguard
docs.text:
Nothing inside a DAT file identifies the mesh it belongs to — no name, no checksum, no topology hash. The only defence is the element count the file declares, so it is checked before any value is read:

  • ND against the dataset's node count
  • NC against its face count

A mismatch raises, reporting both numbers. A file declaring neither count is refused rather than attached on hope.

What this cannot catch: two different meshes with the same node and face counts. Attaching a DAT to the wrong one of those is undetectable from the data, and no driver can fix that — it is a property of the format.

docs.title: Two dialects
docs.text:
Dialect Recognised by Structure New first line is DATASET BEGSCL/BEGVEC groups, ND/NC, NAME, TS <istat> <time>, ENDDS Old no DATASET line one group whose type is the header line (VECTOR ⇒ vector), ND, bare TS <time> blocks; no BEGSCL/ENDDS/NC/NAME

The dialect is decided by the first line alone, exactly as MDAL decides (loadNewFormat vs loadOldFormat). The TS arity differs — new TS <istat> <time>, old TS <time> — so reading an old file with the new arity would take the time for the active flag and the first value for the time, a plausible one-timestep series instead of an error.

The old dialect carries a single node-located group named after the file (it has no NAME card), with no active block (MDAL hardcodes hasStatus false for it). Its ND is checked against the mesh just as the new dialect's counts are.

docs.title: Cards
docs.text:
Card Meaning DATASET marks the new dialect OBJTYPE <type> recorded only; see the location note below BEGSCL / BEGVEC open a scalar / vector group ND <count> / NC <count> declared node / cell counts — the check above NAME <name> the group's name, and so the variable's TIMEUNITS <unit> carried as a time_units variable attribute RT_JULIAN <time> carried as a reference_time variable attribute TS <istat> <time> one timestep; istat means an active block follows ENDDS close the group

A card this driver does not model is ignored, as MDAL ignores the ones it does not model: DAT has accumulated optional cards across SMS versions, and refusing an unknown one would reject files that read fine.

Malformed structure is refused rather than guessed at — a group opened while another is open, an ENDDS with nothing open, a NAME/TIMEUNITS/TS outside a group, a group with no TS at all, a group left unterminated, a short or non-numeric value block, and two groups producing the same variable name.

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• A vector group yields two scalar variables, <name>_x and <name>_y, not one two-component variable. MeshVariable carries a location and a shape over elements and time, with no component axis to put a vector in. Both keep the group name as a prefix so they stay recognisable as one quantity.
  • Values are node-located when ND is declared, which is what SMS writes. A file declaring only NC is read as face-located. With both declared the group is taken as node-located, the SMS convention for BEGSCL/BEGVEC. OBJTYPE is recorded but not used to resolve the location — no SMS writer puts one in it.
  • The active mask becomes a separate face-located variable <name>_active, never folded into the values as NaN (design §21.2). Folding is irreversible and indistinguishable from real missing data. It is deliberately not attached through ParsedVariable.active, because that machinery gives the sibling its parent's location and shape, and a DAT active block counts cells while a node-located group counts nodes.
  • The active block's position is the one thing no vendor file was available to confirm. It is read where MDAL reads it: immediately after the TS card, before the values. A mismatch is made loud rather than silent — the flags must all be 0 or 1, and a block of real values in their place is refused. A file whose node and cell counts are equal defeats that check, which is recorded here because nothing in the data can catch it.
  • RT_JULIAN rides on the variables, not the dataset. attach_data merges the variables a driver returns and keeps the dataset's own global_attributes untouched, so a driver has no route to a file-level attribute. Carrying it properly needs the reference time modelled upstream in pyramids-gis.
  • DAT carries no CRS and no topology, so neither is produced here.
  • There is no lazy path. DAT is plain text with no record index to seek, so the driver does not declare lazy_data and lazy= is accepted and ignored.

Nothing in the file identifies the mesh it belongs to, so ND is checked against the dataset's node count and NC against its face count before any value is read. It is deliberately not attached through ParsedVariable.active: that gives the sibling its parent's location and shape, and a DAT active block counts cells while a node-located group counts nodes.

    import os import tempfile from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset from pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms import ( ... build_minimal_fixture, ... build_minimal_fixture_dat, ... ) with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... mesh_path = os.path.join(directory, "domain.2dm") ... dat_path = os.path.join(directory, "depth.dat") ... build_minimal_fixture(mesh_path) ... build_minimal_fixture_dat(dat_path) ... attached = UgridDataset.read_file(mesh_path).attach_data(dat_path) sorted(attached.data_variable_names) ['depth', 'material', 'node_z'] depth = attached.get("depth") depth.location, depth.shape ('node', (2, 4)) depth.data.tolist() [[0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8], [1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8]]

    from pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms import DatDriver try: ... DatDriver().read("depth.dat") ... except ValueError as error: ... print(str(error).split(";")[0]) dat carries values but no mesh, so it has no read()

    import os import tempfile from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset from pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms import build_minimal_fixture with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory: ... mesh_path = os.path.join(directory, "domain.2dm") ... dat_path = os.path.join(directory, "wrong.dat") ... build_minimal_fixture(mesh_path) ... with open(dat_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle: ... print("DATASET", file=handle) ... print("BEGSCL", file=handle) ... print("ND 9", file=handle) ... print("NAME depth", file=handle) ... print("ENDDS", file=handle) ... try: ... class DatDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the SMS ASCII DAT results format.

    DAT carries values and no topology -- MDAL marks it ``Mesh Frame Support: N/A`` --
    so this driver declares ``needs_mesh`` and implements ``read_data`` instead of
    ``read``. The values attach to a mesh the caller already holds, through
    ``UgridDataset.read_file("domain.2dm").attach_data("depth.dat")``.

    Two dialects are supported. The **new** one opens with a ``DATASET`` card; the
    **old** one has no such line and is recognised by ``SCALAR``, ``VECTOR``, ``TS`` or
    ``TIMEUNITS`` appearing in the file. They differ in ``TS`` arity, which is why the
    distinction is tracked rather than ignored: a parser written only for the new
    dialect reads an old file's *time* as its active flag and silently produces a
    one-timestep series.

    Documented limitations:
        - **The element-count check is the only thing tying a DAT to its mesh.** Nothing
          in the file identifies the mesh it belongs to, so ``ND`` is checked against
          the dataset's node count and ``NC`` against its face count before any value
          is read. A file declaring neither is refused rather than hoped about. Two
          meshes with coincidentally equal counts stay indistinguishable -- a property
          of the format, not of this driver.
        - A ``BEGVEC`` group yields **two scalar variables**, ``<name>_x`` and
          ``<name>_y``, rather than one two-component variable: ``MeshVariable`` carries
          a location and a shape over elements and time, with no component axis for a
          vector. Both keep the group's name as a prefix so they stay recognisable as
          one quantity.
        - Values are **node-located** when ``ND`` is declared, which is what SMS
          writes. A file declaring only ``NC`` is read as face-located. With both
          declared the group is node-located, the SMS convention for
          ``BEGSCL``/``BEGVEC``; ``OBJTYPE`` is recorded but no SMS writer puts a
          location in it.
        - The per-step active mask becomes a **separate face-located variable**
          ``<name>_active``, never folded into the values as NaN (design section 21.2).
          It is deliberately not attached through ``ParsedVariable.active``: that gives
          the sibling its parent's location and shape, and a DAT active block counts
          *cells* while a node-located group counts *nodes*.
        - **The active block is read where MDAL reads it: right after the ``TS`` card,
          before the values.** This is the one part of the layout no vendor file was
          available to confirm, so a mismatch is made loud rather than silent -- the
          flags must all be ``0`` or ``1``, and a block of real values in their place
          is refused. A file whose node and cell counts are equal defeats that check,
          which is recorded here because nothing in the data can catch it.
        - ``RT_JULIAN`` is carried as a ``reference_time`` entry in **each variable's
          attributes**. It cannot reach the dataset's global attributes: ``attach_data``
          merges the variables a driver returns and keeps its own ``global_attributes``
          untouched, so a driver has no way to add one.
        - DAT carries no CRS and no topology, so neither is produced here.

    Examples:
        - Attach a DAT to the mesh it belongs to. Each group arrives as a variable
          carrying the file's time axis:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms import (
            ...     build_minimal_fixture,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_dat,
            ... )
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     mesh_path = os.path.join(directory, "domain.2dm")
            ...     dat_path = os.path.join(directory, "depth.dat")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture(mesh_path)
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_dat(dat_path)
            ...     attached = UgridDataset.read_file(mesh_path).attach_data(dat_path)
            >>> sorted(attached.data_variable_names)
            ['depth', 'material', 'node_z']
            >>> depth = attached.get("depth")
            >>> depth.location, depth.shape
            ('node', (2, 4))
            >>> depth.data.tolist()
            [[0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8], [1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8]]

        - ``read`` is not how a results-only format is reached, and says so rather than
          failing obscurely:

            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms import DatDriver
            >>> try:
            ...     DatDriver().read("depth.dat")
            ... except ValueError as error:
            ...     print(str(error).split(";")[0])
            dat carries values but no mesh, so it has no read()

        - A count disagreeing with the mesh is refused, reporting both numbers, because
          nothing else in the file ties it to a topology:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms import build_minimal_fixture
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     mesh_path = os.path.join(directory, "domain.2dm")
            ...     dat_path = os.path.join(directory, "wrong.dat")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture(mesh_path)
            ...     with open(dat_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            ...         print("DATASET", file=handle)
            ...         print("BEGSCL", file=handle)
            ...         print("ND 9", file=handle)
            ...         print("NAME depth", file=handle)
            ...         print("ENDDS", file=handle)
            ...     try:
            ...         UgridDataset.read_file(mesh_path).attach_data(dat_path)
            ...     except ValueError as error:
            ...         print(str(error).split(": ")[-1])
            declares ND 9 but the mesh has 4 nodes
    """

    name = "dat"
    long_name = "SMS ASCII DAT results"
    suffixes = (".dat",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    # `needs_mesh` is what makes `read_data` the entry point rather than `read`: the
    # format carries no topology, so the mesh has to come from the caller.
    capabilities = frozenset({"needs_mesh", "read_data"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file looks like either DAT dialect.

        The new dialect is a ``DATASET`` first significant line. The old one has no such
        card, so a bounded prefix is scanned for the cards MDAL keys its own old-format
        detection on. Scanning a prefix keeps ``can_open`` cheap on a large results
        file, at the cost of missing a dialect marker buried past the limit -- the same
        bound the 2DM sniff accepts.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when either dialect is recognised.
        """
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            prefix = handle.read(_SNIFF_LIMIT)
        significant = [
            stripped
            for line in prefix.decode("utf-8-sig", errors="replace").splitlines()
            if (stripped := line.strip()) and not stripped.startswith(_COMMENT)
        ]
        if not significant:
            return False
        if significant[0].split()[0].upper() == _DATASET:
            return True
        # The old dialect has no header card, so it is recognised by the cards it must
        # contain. Matching the first token only keeps a file that merely mentions one
        # of those words in a comment or a dataset name from qualifying.
        return any(
            line.split()[0].upper() in _OLD_DIALECT_CARDS for line in significant
        )

    def read(
        self, path: str, *, mesh_name: str | None = None, lazy: bool = True
    ) -> UgridDataset:
        """Refuse the mesh-reading entry point, naming the one to use instead.

        Args:
            path: The results file, named in the message.
            mesh_name: Unused.
            lazy: Unused.

        Returns:
            UgridDataset: Never. The signature matches the driver protocol so the
                refusal is a clear message rather than a ``TypeError``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Always. A results-only format has no topology to return, and an
                empty mesh would be a plausible-looking wrong answer.
        """
        raise ValueError(
            f"{self.name} carries values but no mesh, so it has no read(); attach it to "
            f"a mesh you already have with "
            f"UgridDataset.read_file(mesh_path).attach_data({path!r})"
        )

    def read_data(
        self, path: str, dataset: UgridDataset, *, lazy: bool = True
    ) -> dict[str, MeshVariable]:
        """Read a DAT file's groups as variables for a mesh the caller supplies.

        The declared element counts are checked against ``dataset`` before any value is
        read; the class's documented limitations explain why that check is the whole
        safeguard.

        Args:
            path: The DAT file to read.
            dataset: The mesh the values will attach to, for the element-count check.
            lazy: Accepted for the driver protocol and ignored. DAT is plain text with
                no record index to seek, so there is nothing to defer, and the driver
                does not declare ``lazy_data``.

        Returns:
            dict[str, MeshVariable]: One variable per scalar group, two per vector
                group, plus one ``<name>_active`` face variable per group that carries
                an active mask. The old dialect carries a single group named after the
                file, read node-located with no active block (MDAL's old-format model).

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the file matches neither dialect, a card
                appears outside the group it belongs to, a group opens while one is open
                or ends when none is, a value block is short or non-numeric, two groups
                would produce the same variable name, or an active block holds anything
                but ``0`` and ``1``.
            ValueError: If a declared element count disagrees with ``dataset``, or the
                file declares neither count.
        """
        n_node = int(dataset.mesh.n_node)
        n_face = int(dataset.mesh.n_face)
        if _first_significant_card(path) == _DATASET:
            scan = _DatScan(path, n_node=n_node, n_face=n_face)
            scan.run()
            variables = scan.build()
        else:
            # No DATASET header: the old dialect, which MDAL reads with a separate
            # parser -- one group whose type comes from the header line, ND, and bare
            # TS <time> blocks, with no BEGSCL/ENDDS/NC/NAME cards.
            variables = _DatOldScan(path, n_node=n_node).build()
        return self._build_data_variables(variables, dataset.mesh_name)

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

def can_open(self, path: str) -> bool:
    """Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

    A missing path or a directory answers ``False``, and so does a suffix this
    driver does not claim. Everything about the file's *content* is the subclass's
    ``_sniff`` to judge, and the default ``_sniff`` judges nothing -- so on
    ``BaseDriver`` itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers ``True``. A
    driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature,
    as :meth:`~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff` does.

    declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only ``_sniff``
    sits inside that guard: a ``TypeError`` from being handed something that is not
    a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

    Args:
        path: The filesystem path to test.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` only when the suffix matches and ``_sniff`` accepts the file.

          default ``_sniff``, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file
          under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:

            >>> import tempfile

            ...     name = "tiny"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            >>> driver = TinyDriver()
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     empty = os.path.join(directory, "empty.tiny")
            ...     open(empty, "wb").close()

            ...         driver.can_open(os.path.join(directory, "gone.tiny")),
            ...         driver.can_open(directory),

          driver named, so one broken candidate cannot abort dispatch for the rest:

            >>> import tempfile

            >>> class BrokenSniffDriver(BaseDriver):
            ...     name = "broken"
            ...     suffixes = (".tiny",)
            ...
            ...     def _sniff(self, path):
            ...         raise RuntimeError("header parser is wrong")
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "f.tiny")
            ...     with open(path, "wb") as handle:
            ...         _ = handle.write(b"anything at all")

def read_data(
    self, path: str, dataset: UgridDataset, *, lazy: bool = True
) -> dict[str, MeshVariable]:
    """Read a DAT file's groups as variables for a mesh the caller supplies.

    The declared element counts are checked against ``dataset`` before any value is
    read; the class's documented limitations explain why that check is the whole
    safeguard.

    Args:
        path: The DAT file to read.
        dataset: The mesh the values will attach to, for the element-count check.
        lazy: Accepted for the driver protocol and ignored. DAT is plain text with
            no record index to seek, so there is nothing to defer, and the driver
            does not declare ``lazy_data``.

    Returns:
        dict[str, MeshVariable]: One variable per scalar group, two per vector
            group, plus one ``<name>_active`` face variable per group that carries
            an active mask. The old dialect carries a single group named after the
            file, read node-located with no active block (MDAL's old-format model).

    Raises:
        FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the file matches neither dialect, a card
            appears outside the group it belongs to, a group opens while one is open
            or ends when none is, a value block is short or non-numeric, two groups
            would produce the same variable name, or an active block holds anything
            but ``0`` and ``1``.
        ValueError: If a declared element count disagrees with ``dataset``, or the
            file declares neither count.
    """
    n_node = int(dataset.mesh.n_node)
    n_face = int(dataset.mesh.n_face)
    if _first_significant_card(path) == _DATASET:
        scan = _DatScan(path, n_node=n_node, n_face=n_face)
        scan.run()
        variables = scan.build()
    else:
        # No DATASET header: the old dialect, which MDAL reads with a separate
        # parser -- one group whose type comes from the header line, ND, and bare
        # TS <time> blocks, with no BEGSCL/ENDDS/NC/NAME cards.
        variables = _DatOldScan(path, n_node=n_node).build()
    return self._build_data_variables(variables, dataset.mesh_name)

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• The projection field and the node-record column order are read as MDAL reads them, but could not be checked against a vendor file. If a real Mike21 mesh orders its node columns differently, the coordinates would be wrong in a plausible way. This is the part of the driver a vendor sample should confirm — tracked for the vendor_data suite.
  • The projection is mapped to a CRS only when it is real. A WKT string or an EPSG code the vendored PROJ validates is carried; a DHI-internal name such as UTM-32 or LONG/LAT carries no datum and leaves crs as None rather than being guessed at. Validation is what tells the two apart — the field is not trusted for being present.
  • Node elevation becomes a node_z variable, as it does for 2DM: the pyramids mesh model is planar and carries no per-node elevation coordinate (design §6). The z column is read as written, never fabricated.
  • The boundary code is not carried. It marks open and land boundaries, which this package has nowhere to put on a bare frame; it is dropped rather than turned into a variable the mesh model would not recognise.
  • Node ids are resolved through an id map rather than assumed contiguous, so a renumbered file is wired correctly; the 1-based numbering is recorded for a writer to restore.
  • Frame only. The format carries no results, so there are no time-varying variables and no write support yet (write arrives with W4).

    """Reader for the DHI Mike21 ``.mesh`` frame format.

    Plain text despite the DHI name, so it needs no dependency. A header line, then one
    record per node, then an element header, then one record per element. The format
    carries a mesh frame and no results, so the driver declares ``read_mesh`` only.

    Node elevation becomes a ``node_z`` variable, as it does for 2DM: the pyramids mesh
    model is planar and carries no per-node elevation coordinate (design section 6). The
    file's z column is read as written, never fabricated.

    Documented limitations:
        - **The projection field and the node-record column order are read as MDAL
          reads them, but could not be checked against a vendor file.** If a real Mike21
          mesh orders its node columns differently, the coordinates would be wrong in a
          plausible way; this is the part of the driver a vendor sample should confirm.
        - **The projection is mapped to a CRS only when it is real.** A WKT string or an
          EPSG code that the vendored PROJ validates is carried; a DHI-internal name
          such as ``UTM-32`` or ``LONG/LAT`` carries no datum and leaves ``crs`` as
          ``None`` rather than being guessed at.

          land boundaries, which this package has nowhere to put on a bare frame; it is
          dropped rather than turned into a variable the mesh model would not recognise.
        - A triangle in a quad mesh is padded with a trailing ``0`` node id. Since ids
          are 1-based, ``0`` is read as fill and becomes ``-1`` padding, never node
          index zero.

          renumbered file is wired correctly; the 1-based numbering is recorded for a

          triangles come through as a 2D mesh, and the 1-based ids arrive 0-based with
          the file's base recorded for a writer:

            ...     Mike21Driver,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_mike21,

            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "domain.mesh")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_mike21(path)
            ...     dataset = Mike21Driver().read(path)
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (4, 2)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2], [0, 2, 3]]
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.original_start_index
            1

          per-node elevation coordinate:

            ...     Mike21Driver,

            ... )

    long_name = "DHI Mike21 mesh"
    suffixes = (".mesh",)

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the first line parses as a Mike21 header.

        The header is ``<item> <unit> <node_count> <projection...>``, so a readable
        first line whose third field is a positive integer is the cheapest signature
        the format offers. A binary file decodes to replacement characters and fails
        that test rather than raising.

        ``.mesh`` is a common suffix, so the sniff is what keeps a foreign ``.mesh``
        file -- a 3D model export, say -- from being claimed. It is still only a header
        shape: a file that passes it but breaks later is refused by ``read``, which is
        why the two must not disagree about what a header looks like.

        Args:
            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when the first line has the header's shape.
        """
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            first = handle.readline(4096)
        tokens = first.decode("utf-8-sig", errors="replace").split()
        if len(tokens) < _ELEMENT_HEADER_FIELDS + 1:
            return False
        try:
            return int(tokens[2]) > 0
        except ValueError:
            return False

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a Mike21 ``.mesh`` file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The ``.mesh`` file to read.
            lazy: Ignored -- the format is plain text and read eagerly.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: Nodes, faces and the ``node_z`` elevation variable.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the file is empty, a record is short of its
                columns, a count does not match the records that follow, or a numeric
                field is not a number.
            ValueError: If an element references a node id the file never defined, or
                two nodes share an id.
        """
        return _Mike21Scan(path).build()

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• A round trip is not geometrically faithful. z survives as a node_z variable, but pyramids' mesh model is planar, so a consumer reading the geometry sees the (x, y) projection. This is inherent to carrying a 3D surface in a 2D model (design §6).
  • The whole file is read eagerly. A PLY from a 3D scanner can be large; there is no record index to seek, so every vertex property and face is read at once. The driver does not declare lazy_data.
  • Extra vertex properties become node variables. Colours, normals and the like are carried as their own node-located variables rather than dropped.
  • Faces may be triangles, quads or mixed; short rows pad to the widest with -1. A face of fewer than three vertices (an edge or a point) is refused.
  • PLY carries no CRS and no units, so crs is None. Indices are 0-based and stay so.

Reads ASCII and both binary byte orders. A PLY is a geometry format with elevation per vertex and no time axis, so z becomes a node_z variable and any other vertex property (colours, normals) becomes its own node-located variable rather than being dropped.

Documented limitations

  • The whole file is read eagerly. A PLY from a 3D scanner can be large; there is no record index to seek, so every vertex property and face is read at once. The driver does not declare lazy_data.
  • Faces may be triangles, quads or mixed; short rows are padded to the widest with -1. A PLY edge or point element (a face of fewer than three vertices) is refused, since it is not a surface.
  • PLY carries no CRS and no units, so crs is None.
  • Face indices are 0-based in PLY, and stay 0-based.

class PlyDriver(BaseDriver):
    """Reader for the Stanford PLY polygon format.

    Reads ASCII and both binary byte orders. A PLY is a geometry format with elevation
    per vertex and no time axis, so ``z`` becomes a ``node_z`` variable and any other
    vertex property (colours, normals) becomes its own node-located variable rather than
    being dropped.

    Documented limitations:
        - **A round trip is not geometrically faithful.** ``z`` survives as node data, but
          pyramids' mesh model is planar, so a consumer reading the geometry sees the
          ``(x, y)`` projection. This is inherent to carrying a 3D surface in a 2D model
          (design section 6).
        - **The whole file is read eagerly.** A PLY from a 3D scanner can be large; there
          is no record index to seek, so every vertex property and face is read at once.
          The driver does not declare ``lazy_data``.
        - Faces may be triangles, quads or mixed; short rows are padded to the widest with
          ``-1``. A PLY edge or point element (a face of fewer than three vertices) is
          refused, since it is not a surface.
        - PLY carries no CRS and no units, so ``crs`` is ``None``.
        - Face indices are 0-based in PLY, and stay 0-based.

    Examples:
        - Write a small ASCII PLY and read it back. The vertex z becomes ``node_z`` and
          the faces come through 0-based:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.interchange import (
            ...     PlyDriver,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_ply,
            ... )
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "surface.ply")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_ply(path)
            ...     dataset = PlyDriver().read(path)
            >>> dataset.mesh.n_node, dataset.mesh.n_face
            (4, 2)
            >>> dataset.mesh.face_node_connectivity.data.tolist()
            [[0, 1, 2], [0, 2, 3]]
            >>> dataset.get("node_z").data.tolist()
            [2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5]
    """

    name = "ply"
    long_name = "Stanford PLY"
    suffixes = (".ply",)
    api_version = MESH_DRIVER_API_VERSION
    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "read_data"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file opens with the ``ply`` magic line."""
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            first = handle.readline().strip()
        return first == _PLY_MAGIC

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a PLY file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:
            path: The PLY file to read.
            lazy: Ignored -- a PLY has no record index to seek, so it is read eagerly.

        Returns:
            ParsedMesh: Nodes, faces, ``node_z`` and any extra vertex-property variables.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: On a missing or malformed header, an unknown
                property type, a face of fewer than three vertices, or a truncated body.
        """
        return _PlyReader(path).build()

Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

docs.text:
The TELEMAC Selafin reader, and the package's first binary driver. Fortran unformatted records with an undeclared byte order and an optional double-precision variant. It proves the lazy path: the topology and the one-float time records are read eagerly, and each variable's per-timestep slab is left behind a loader that seeks straight to it.

Driver name selafin Suffixes .slf, .srf, .ser, .sel Capabilities read_mesh, read_data, lazy_data Extra required none Returns UgridDataset 
from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid import UgridDataset

dataset = UgridDataset.read_file("model.slf")
depth = dataset.get("WATER DEPTH").data   # read now; deferred until this line

docs.title: How it is read
docs.text:
• Byte order is detected, not declared. The first record must announce an 80-byte title in one order or the other; a file that does neither is not Selafin.
  • Precision comes from the title marker. SERAFIND is double precision, SERAFIN single, and the width applies to every float record — coordinates and data alike.
  • Variable names are 32 characters, split by position into a 16-char name and a 16-char unit. Splitting on whitespace instead would lose a multi-word name's tail.
  • IKLE connectivity is 1-based; it arrives 0-based, with the base recorded for a writer to restore.

docs.title: Documented limitations
docs.text:
• The coordinate origin is applied, and getting it wrong is undetectable. IPARAM[2] and IPARAM[3] are the x and y origins the stored coordinates are offsets from; they are added to the node coordinates. Read without adding them, the mesh sits near zero instead of at its real location — plausible and completely wrong, with nothing in the data to catch it.
  • A layered 3D file is refused. IPARAM[6] is the plane count; 0 and 1 both mean 2D, and a value above 1 is a real 3D file. Its NPOIN and prism IKLE cannot be read as a flat 2D mesh without returning all planes' nodes under 6-node faces, and a faithful surface extraction needs a vendor file to verify the plane ordering, so it is refused — as MDAL refuses it. A full 3D read needs the layered mesh model pyramids does not have yet (design §21.1).
  • A parallel sub-domain file is refused. A non-zero interface-point count (IPARAM[8]) means local numbering within one partition, so the connectivity would index a sub-domain rather than the whole mesh. It is keyed on interface points alone — the boundary-point field is a mesh property, nonzero for ordinary serial meshes. Merge the partitions before reading.
  • Variables are node-located, always — never inferred from an array length.
  • The IKLE row/column order could not be checked against a vendor file. It is read row-major (one element's NDP node ids contiguous), as MDAL reads it. A real file that stored it transposed would give a scrambled mesh; this is the detail a vendor sample should confirm, tracked for the vendor_data suite.
  • A partial final timestep is dropped with a warning — a run killed mid-write leaves a dangling time record, and only whole steps are read.
  • There is no CRS in the format, so crs is None; it is never inferred from the coordinate magnitudes.

    first record length (see :func:`~pyramids_mesh._binary.detect_endianness`). The file
    carries a mesh and node-located results over time, so the driver declares
    ``read_mesh``, ``read_data`` and ``lazy_data``: the topology and the one-float time
    records are read eagerly, and each variable's per-timestep slab is left behind a
    loader that seeks to it.

    Documented limitations:
        - **The coordinate origin is applied, and getting it wrong is undetectable.**
          ``IPARAM[2]`` and ``IPARAM[3]`` are the x and y origins the stored coordinates
          are offsets from; they are added to the node coordinates. A file with a
          non-zero origin read without adding it gives a mesh sitting near zero instead
          of in its real location -- plausible and completely wrong, with nothing in the
          data to catch it.
        - **Single versus double precision applies to every float record.** The title's
          format marker (``SERAFIND`` double, ``SERAFIN`` single) sets the width for the
          coordinates and every data slab alike; reading the wrong width desynchronises
          the file, which the trailing-length-word check then reports.
        - **A layered 3D file is refused.** ``IPARAM[6]`` is the plane count; 0 and 1 both
          mean 2D (some tools write 1 for 2D), and a value above 1 is a real 3D file whose
          ``NPOIN`` and prism ``IKLE`` cannot be read as a flat 2D mesh without returning
          all planes' nodes under 6-node faces. A full 3D read needs the layered mesh
          model pyramids does not have yet (design section 21.1), so the file is refused
          -- as MDAL refuses it -- rather than yielding a plausible, wrong mesh.
        - **A parallel sub-domain file is refused.** A non-zero interface-point count
          (``IPARAM[8]``) means local numbering within one partition, so the connectivity
          would index a sub-domain rather than the whole mesh. It is keyed on interface
          points alone -- the boundary-point field is a mesh property, nonzero for
          ordinary serial meshes, and keying on it would refuse them.
        - **Selafin variables are node-located, always.** The location is not inferred
          from an array length.

          read row-major -- one element's ``NDP`` node ids contiguous -- as MDAL reads
          it. A real file that stores it transposed would give a scrambled mesh; this is
          the detail a vendor sample should confirm.
        - There is no CRS in the format, so ``crs`` is ``None``; it is never inferred
          from the coordinate magnitudes.

    Examples:
        - Write the smallest valid Selafin file and read it back. The 1-based ``IKLE``
          arrives 0-based, with the file's base recorded for a writer:

            >>> import os
            >>> import tempfile
            >>> from pyramids_mesh.drivers.telemac import (
            ...     SelafinDriver,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_selafin,
            ... )
            >>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "model.slf")

            ...     SelafinDriver,
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_selafin,
            ... )

            ...     path = os.path.join(directory, "model.slf")
            ...     build_minimal_fixture_selafin(path)
            ...     dataset = SelafinDriver().read(path)
            ...     variable = dataset.get("WATER DEPTH")
            ...     location, shape, units = (
            ...         variable.location,
            ...         variable.shape,
            ...         variable.units,
            ...     )
            ...     second_step = variable.data[1].tolist()

            >>> second_step

    long_name = "TELEMAC Selafin / Serafin"
    suffixes = (".slf", ".srf", ".ser", ".sel")

    capabilities = frozenset({"read_mesh", "read_data", "lazy_data"})

    def _sniff(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Report whether the file is a Selafin file, by the endianness probe.

        The first record must declare an 80-byte title in one byte order or the other.
        That probe is cheap and definitive, so it is the whole sniff; a file failing it
        is not Selafin.

            path: The file to inspect.

        Returns:
            bool: ``True`` when the endianness probe succeeds.
        """
        try:
            detect_endianness(path, expect_first_record=_TITLE_LENGTH)
        except ValueError:
            return False
        return True

    def _parse(self, path: str, *, lazy: bool) -> ParsedMesh:
        """Read a Selafin file into a :class:`ParsedMesh`.

        Args:

                ``False``, read every value now.

            ParsedMesh: Nodes, faces and the node-located variables.

        Raises:
            FileFormatNotSupportedError: If the file is not Selafin, declares a parallel
                sub-domain, or is truncated against the counts its header promises.

        return _SelafinReader(path, lazy=lazy).build()

docs.title: can_open(path)
docs.text:
Report whether this driver recognises the file, without ever raising.

A missing path or a directory answers False, and so does a suffix this driver does not claim. Everything about the file's content is the subclass's _sniff to judge, and the default _sniff judges nothing -- so on BaseDriver itself an empty file with a claimed suffix answers True. A driver that means to decline an empty or foreign file reads a header signature, as :meth:~pyramids_mesh.drivers.sms.TwoDmDriver._sniff does.

A _sniff that fails for any reason is reported as a warning and the file declined, so a broken candidate cannot abort driver dispatch. Only _sniff sits inside that guard: a TypeError from being handed something that is not a path is the caller's mistake, not a verdict about a file, so it propagates.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str

The filesystem path to test.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True only when the suffix matches and _sniff accepts the file.

Examples:

  • The path checks and the suffix are all the base class decides. With the default _sniff, which accepts whatever reaches it, an empty file under a claimed suffix is recognised and a missing one is not:
